summary: In Canvas Builder's sandbox mode the HTTP client talks to the gateway and to nothing else, and every change it sends can carry a job label. client.Client gains Sandbox, JobLabel and Notices; New attaches the workspace profile and narrows the HTTP client to it; doInternal checks the target URL before it builds anything and puts X-Job-Label on the request. The CLI gains the persistent --job flag and validates its value. A new test-only package, internal/gatewaytest, stands in for cb-gateway and for the course workspace around it.
reason:
Task 1 validated Canvas Builder's settings and attached a sandbox.Profile to the config. Nothing read it yet, so the base URL was checked once at load and never again. Three things could still send the agent token somewhere else: a caller setting c.BaseURL after New, a redirect the gateway (or anything answering on its port) returns, and later tasks' own URLs -- an upload_url, a file url, a Link next page. All three go through one seam now, Client.CheckURL, which is nil outside sandbox mode and otherwise refuses anything that isn't the gateway, naming only the scheme and host because a file URL's path and query carry a verifier.

CheckURL sits in doInternal right after targetURL is built, before the body is marshalled, before the auth header is minted and before the dry-run branch. A refused URL therefore never reaches a credential store or a socket, which is what ADR 0001 asks for: the agent can read files and set variables, so the CLI must fail before it can be useful to a redirected target.

The redirect check wraps the generated CheckRedirect rather than replacing it. The generated one re-derives auth per hop and strips Authorization on a cross-host hop; both still happen, after the gateway rule has had its say. Order matters: on a hop off the gateway the request must fail, not merely lose its header.

The HTTP timeout is raised to Profile.HTTPTimeout(--timeout) in the same place. The gateway's approvals.Broker.Ask denies a held approval the moment the client's context ends, so a CLI whose timeout is shorter than the approval window turns every slow approval into a denial. Doing it in New rather than at each call site means no command can get this wrong.

X-Job-Label goes on after the per-endpoint header overrides, so an endpoint can't shadow it, and on every request rather than only on writes: a read carrying the label costs nothing and lets Canvas Builder show what a job looked at. An unlabelled write still goes out (decision D2) with MsgNoJobLabel written to Notices once per Client -- a missing label costs the instructor a grouped Undo, while refusing the write would cost them the work, and repeating the notice per request would bury the result.

Notices exists because a message for the agent isn't part of the result. It defaults to os.Stderr through an accessor rather than being set in New, so a Client built by hand (several tests do) still prints somewhere real.

internal/gatewaytest is a package rather than a helper file because Tasks 2 to 9 all need it and it has to be importable from both client and cli; it imports neither, so there is no cycle. Its Workspace helper writes the same layout the app writes -- config/config.toml, data/credentials.toml at 0600, workspace.json, materials/ -- and clears CANVAS_CONFIG, CANVAS_BASE_URL, both token variables, the four CANVAS_*_DIR variables, the four XDG_* variables and HOME. HOME is not in the plan's list but has to be cleared: the config loader falls back to $HOME/.config/canvas-pp-cli, which is how a developer's own Canvas leaked into a Task 1 test.

A refusal is marked so the retry loop can tell it apart from a failed connection. CheckRedirect's error comes back out of http.Client.Do wrapped in a *url.Error, and doInternal's transport-error branch treats every non-context error as transient: it set lastErr and continued. A redirect off the gateway therefore sent the first hop to the gateway four times, which for a PUT, POST or DELETE means the gateway saw the write four times and could have asked the instructor to approve it four times. The wrapper returns a *refusalError, and the loop returns it unwrapped on the first attempt, so the message the agent reads is the refusal rather than net/http's envelope around it.
known_limitations:
CheckURL compares scheme and host only, which is what "Allowed" means. A path on the gateway is not checked here; the gateway itself decides what an agent may reach, and Task 5 narrows the command surface so the agent is not offered paths that will be refused.

The redirect rule is enforced in CheckRedirect, so it runs per hop but not on the first request's own URL -- that is CheckURL's job in doInternal. Any future code path that builds a request without going through doInternal has to call CheckURL itself. Tasks 6 to 8 do exactly that for upload_url, a file url and a Link next page.

--job is validated in newClient, which is where every command gets its client, so a command that never builds one (version, help) accepts the flag silently. Nothing acts on it there, so this costs nothing beyond a quiet flag.

An unlabelled write warns once per Client, not once per process. A single CLI invocation builds one client, so in practice these are the same; a future command that builds two would warn twice.

Nothing yet maps a gateway refusal onto exit code 9 or an unknown outcome onto 8, and the retry loop still retries a write whose outcome is unknown. Those are Tasks 3 and 4.

gatewaytest.Fake matches a method and path exactly and answers anything else with a 404 in Canvas's error shape. That is deliberate -- an unexpected request fails its test rather than passing quietly -- but it means a test that needs query-dependent behaviour has to branch inside its own handler.
validated_outcome:
go vet ./... clean, go test ./... passing on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1, and go test -race ./internal/client/ passing.

New coverage in internal/client/sandbox_test.go, each built from a real config.Load of a gatewaytest workspace so the profile is attached the way a real run attaches it: a 302 off the gateway fails with the NotGateway wording, the other server sees no request and the message doesn't contain the token; a 302 to another path on the gateway is followed and the second hop still carries Authorization: Bearer tA; a BaseURL changed after New is refused with nothing sent anywhere; an approval timeout of 1s with --timeout 200ms gives an HTTP timeout of 31s and a PUT the gateway holds for 1.5s succeeds; a job label of "Déplacer — مقرر" arrives byte for byte and an empty label sends no header at all; two unlabelled PUTs both reach the gateway with the notice printed once, while a read and anything in normal mode print nothing; a GET with params and a PUT with a form body both carry the token only in Authorization, never in the query or the body; and a client with no profile still follows a cross-host redirect with Authorization stripped, which is the upstream behaviour.

internal/cli/joblabel_test.go covers a plain and an accented label, an empty and a blank one, a newline, a tab, and 100 versus 101 runes.

golangci-lint reports nothing in internal/gatewaytest, internal/client/sandbox.go, internal/cli/joblabel.go or either new test. The repo's `make lint` still fails on roughly 700 pre-existing findings in the generated internal/cli and internal/client packages, which this patch neither adds to nor fixes.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch and raised one finding, the retried redirect refusal above. It was real: a test asserting one PUT reached the gateway saw four before the fix and one after.
